findings.title: resolve_output_dir/get_output_path are dead code with a docstring that describes machinery this same branch deleted
findings.suggested_fix: Delete resolve_output_dir() (line 381) and get_output_path() (line 407); neither is called by any production code path -- get_base_output/run_outputs now read output_dir from the manifest instead (utils.py:397-405, :721-733). The docstring also claims the function is 'shared with the importer's scan so the reader and the scan cannot disagree' but the importer's scan (scan_roots/describe_importable_run/scan_importable_runs) was removed in this same diff, so the stated reason for keeping it no longer applies.

findings.title: _require_model_run_path is unreachable from production code; the docstring and a test still describe it as 'the funnel'
findings.suggested_fix: Every production caller of a run path now goes through _require_run_entry/_run_entry (utils.py:200-224), which resolve against run_store.list_runs() and legacy uuids. _require_model_run_path and the _get_model_run_path_by_id it wraps are no longer called by controllers.py or any other production module -- only by tests/test_registry_listing.py:94 and tests/test_endpoint_parity.py:139, the latter's docstring literally claiming 'Every path build funnels through _require_model_run_path; keep the funnel', which is no longer true. Either delete the function and its test, or delete _run_entry-based duplication and go back to one funnel -- keeping both invites the two to drift (e.g. only _run_entry currently sees unusable/legacy-uuid runs).

findings.title: removeModelRun only catches OSError, but delete() can now fail through the S3 backend with a different exception type
findings.suggested_fix: run_store.delete() (run_store.py:414-441) now deletes through either a local filesystem (shutil.rmtree, raises OSError) or an object-storage backend (_delete_prefix -> backend.listdir/backend.delete, which on django-storages' S3Storage surfaces botocore.exceptions.ClientError on a real failure such as denied permissions or a network error, not OSError). removeModelRun's except OSError clause (controllers.py:274-278) only covers the local case; an S3 delete failure would propagate as an unhandled exception and produce Django's generic 500 instead of the intended JSON error. Catch a broader/backend-specific exception, or have run_store.delete wrap backend failures in a common exception the controller already handles. No test exercises a failing S3 delete (tests/test_run_removal.py has no such case).

findings.title: Reading unconverted (.nc) t-route output over object storage will raise inside xarray with no friendly degrade path; the only guard against it lives in a developer script
findings.suggested_fix: _normalised_troute_frame falls back to xr.open_dataset(source) when troute output was never converted to parquet/csv (utils.py:330-335). Over object storage, `source` is built as an s3:// URI (get_troute_df -> _child, utils.py:355-374), which plain xarray cannot open. Every other unusable state (schema version, missing outputs) is caught and reported through run_store._describe's `reason` field (run_store.py:251-286); this one is not, so a run migrated to S3 without reconversion produces an unhandled exception in getTrouteTimeSeries/getTrouteVariables (controllers.py has no except clause for it) rather than a clear message. Today the only place this invariant is enforced is scripts/try-object-storage.sh's TROUTE_FORMAT check (lines 64-81), a local rehearsal script -- it never runs against a production deployment. Move the check into manifest.distill/_describe (e.g. mark a run unusable when backend is object storage and troute.format is .nc/.csv) so the guard applies wherever the app actually runs.

findings.title: Most environment variables this branch introduces are undocumented in README.md
findings.suggested_fix: README.md's 'Hosted deployments' section (line 97-104) documents only NGIAB_STORAGE_BACKEND and the ngiab_runs STORAGES alias. This branch also introduces NGIAB_MANAGED_ROOT, NGIAB_RUNS_PREFIX, NGIAB_LISTING_TTL_SECONDS, NGIAB_S3_BUCKET, NGIAB_S3_ENDPOINT, NGIAB_S3_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT and DUCKDB_HOME (run_store.py:40,55,60; controllers.py:347; duckdb_conn.py:78; conf/portal-config.d/20-object-storage.sh) with none mentioned in README.md, even though conf/portal-config.d/20-object-storage.sh and scripts/try-object-storage.sh both depend on several of them to actually stand up the S3 path an operator would use. Add a short reference table (name, default, when it matters) to the hosted-deployments section.

findings.title: Two name-validation rules split across modules, one referenced only by a comment naming a private symbol
findings.suggested_fix: run_store._is_plain_name (run_store.py:444-446, containment: one path component) and ingest.NAME_PATTERN/is_valid_name (ingest.py:54-59, a stricter charset for names chosen at upload time) encode genuinely different invariants and the split itself is defensible -- but ingest.py:50 documents the relationship only in a comment that names run_store's private function by string, with no import or test tying the two together. If _is_plain_name is ever renamed or its containment rule changes, this comment goes stale silently. Consider a short cross-reference test (e.g. every name is_valid_name accepts is also accepted by run_store._is_plain_name) so the two are demonstrably scoped correctly rather than by comment alone.

findings.title: get_base_output duplicates run_outputs' directory resolution and is now called only by tests
findings.suggested_fix: get_base_output(model_id) (utils.py:397-405) and run_outputs(model_run_id) (utils.py:721-733) compute the same `_child(entry['path'], document.get('output_dir') or _DEFAULT_OUTPUT_SUBDIR)` expression independently. controllers.py imports run_outputs, not get_base_output; the latter is exercised only by tests/test_endpoint_parity.py:147,152. Consider having run_outputs call get_base_output (or delete get_base_output and point the tests at run_outputs().directory) so there is one place this path is built.

residual_risks: run_store <-> duckdb_conn is a real import cycle broken by a function-local import inside duckdb_conn._authenticate (duckdb_conn.py:122-132). It works today and is well documented, but nothing prevents a future edit from moving that import to module scope and reintroducing a circular-import failure at Django app-loading time; a lightweight import-order test would catch that regression before it reaches production.

conf/portal-config.d/20-object-storage.sh writes Django's STORAGES setting from NGIAB_S3_* variables, and run_store._borrowed_from_default reads that same STORAGES entry back -- so the two cannot disagree about bucket/credentials by construction. This is sound, but it is a non-obvious one-way relationship (shell script writes, Python reads) that is easy to break by editing one side without realizing the other depends on its exact OPTIONS keys (bucket_name, endpoint_url, access_key, secret_key, region_name).
testing_gaps: No test exercises run_store.delete()/removeModelRun against the object-storage backend when the backend raises a non-OSError exception (e.g., a permission error from S3 delete).
No test exercises reading unconverted (.nc or .csv) t-route output when NGIAB_STORAGE_BACKEND=s3, i.e. the failure mode scripts/try-object-storage.sh's TROUTE_FORMAT guard exists to avoid.

tests/test_endpoint_parity.py still asserts that _require_model_run_path is 'the funnel' every path build goes through, but production code no longer routes through it -- the test is exercising dead code and its docstring's claim should be re-verified against current wiring.
